Let's say I'm walking down the street and a guy comes up and demands my phone, wallet, etc. and let's say I can't get to my firearm without setting this guy off and causing him to shoot me. I hand over my stuff and he turns and runs away. If I draw and fire on him, after he's mugged me, what's the legal repercussion? Does anybody know of cases similar to this scenario that I can read or know of any precendents already set by the court?

Every jurisdiction may have slightly different rules but speaking very generally and assuming no other facts which would alter the details here, you'd be guilty of second degree murder or voluntary manslaughter. (Side note: your publicly asking this question could possibly be used to establish premeditation in a push to convict you of first degree murder.) You're allowed to use lethal force to defend against imminent risk of death or grievous bodily harm. If he's running away, he's no longer a threat.

I'm not worried about being brought up on murder charges...I haven't done anything, just asking a question because I wondered how that worked

Thanks

Typically speaking, this is considered 2nd degree murder or voluntary manslaughter, as the other comment pointed out. In every state I'm familiar with, you have to be in immediate danger to be legally able to shoot someone.

To prevent this from happening, ALWAYS keep your weapon in an accessible location. Personally I carry a .40 subcompact in my front pocket, and if ever confronted I just keep one hand in the air while slowly reaching to that pocket, and once my hand is on the grip, that's when I move as quickly as possible to bring aim onto my assailant. This has happened twice to me in the current city I'm living in, and both times the would-be robber just turned tail and ran.

Any situation where the threat has ended and you shoot would put you as the criminal. Leaving a scene to grab a weapon and returning would also land you in trouble. Shooting a burglar as they exit your house is a no no. Basically, don't shoot unless you could die in that immediate moment. Source: was cop. Do not take this as advice on how to kill someone. Taking someone's life is no small thing. You should always exhaust every other means of stopping an immediate threat, as deadly force is a last resort.

Just in case anyone reading this doesn't already have an understanding of this.
